# Per-fixture overrides for test_transform_oracle.rs.
#
# This file currently declares NO overrides, and
# `parses_committed_overrides_file` asserts that it stays that way: every
# fixture in every oracle corpus has its forward golden, inverse golden,
# round-trip and .map/.simp equivalence checks enabled, at the harness's
# default tolerances.
#
# The syntax below is retained because the parser supports it and a future
# fixture may need it. Any entry added here must carry a comment saying what
# is disabled and why, and must be counted in PLAN.md §6.
#
# Round-trip lines (GRID-domain corpora: .head, .ast).  The round-trip
# check asserts inverse(forward(P)) recovers the pixel P within an
# absolute pixel tolerance (default 0.05 px):
#   <relpath> off              disable the round-trip check for this fixture
#   <relpath> <rtol> <atol>    use a looser per-fixture tolerance
#
# Golden lines.  The golden check compares live outputs against the
# recorded oracle values:
#   <relpath> golden off       skip golden comparison, both directions
#   <relpath> golden-fwd off   skip golden comparison, forward sections
#   <relpath> golden-inv off   skip golden comparison, inverse sections
# Use these only for sections whose recorded values sit on a mathematical
# singularity and are not architecture-stable; every skip needs a comment
# explaining why.
#
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.

# Rows where C's own recorded inverse does not recover the pixel are excused
# per row by RTRIP_REFERENCE_GAPS_LICENSED in test_transform_oracle.rs, not by
# an entry here: tnx-cheb.head (all 24 rows) and tsc.head (row 10, a 360 deg
# alias in an image wider than the quad-cube period, which the alias-aware
# check accepts on its own anyway).

# Two rows of that fixture's inverse section are substituted per row by
# FMA_SUBSTITUTIONS_LICENSED in test_transform_oracle.rs, which asserts the
# value C's own source prescribes rather than the fused one the generator host
# recorded.  The other 22 rows are compared as normal.
